answers.question: How long before I can run again? A friend wants me to race the Thanksgiving 10K in five weeks.
answers.answer:
You can jog again once walking feels normal and the quad soreness is gone, usually 7 to 10 days after a marathon. Expect that to be late this week or early next, starting with 20 to 30 minutes very easy and only if nothing is sharp.

The Thanksgiving 10K in five weeks is doable, but treat it as a fun tune-up, not a personal best attempt. A rough shape: this week walk and one or two short jogs, next week ease back to 20 to 25 miles of easy running, then two normal weeks with one light workout each, then a short sharpening week into race day. If you want to actually race a 10K hard, I would rather pick one in January or February and build properly.

Tell me what you want after that so I can plan beyond these two reset weeks.

new.analysis:
## What the week showed
You executed the race plan almost exactly as drawn up: easy Tue, the short marathon-pace tune-up Wed, shakeout Fri, and the marathon on Sun. Splits held 8:30 pace through 33 miles before the quads cried uncle, which is a classic late-race fade, not a pacing mistake. A 12-minute PR off 40-mile peak weeks is a strong return on the build.

## Why this week is almost all rest
A marathon leaves micro-damage in the legs that takes one to three weeks to fully clear, and running on top of it just drags out the soreness. The old rule of thumb is one easy day per mile raced before any real training, so you are looking at mid-November before structured work. The two short jogs below are only if the legs feel ready; if they don't, swap them for a walk and nothing is lost.

## What I need from you
Have a think about what you want next. Options I'd flag: a short winter break then a spring half, another marathon in the spring at a sharper target, or a 5K/10K block over the winter to build speed. Your answer shapes the next 8 to 12 weeks, and we have time to decide, no rush.
